phase3_findings.summary: The #1527 fix name-scopes sw_attempted (keys on tool_use NAME) but leaves sw_denied keying on the whole serialized denial record — the identical input-JSON false-positive vector on the side that actually gates shipping.
phase3_findings.detail: collect() does denials.append(json.dumps(d)) (full record), and compute_verdict does sw_denied = 'schedulewakeup' in denial_text. If any tool's permission_denials record carries the token 'ScheduleWakeup' in a nested input/query field (e.g. a denied ToolSearch 'select:ScheduleWakeup'), sw_denied fires falsely -> REMOVED (no attempt) or DENIED (attempt) -> flag ships though the tool was available. This is the exact false-positive class #1527 hardened on the attempt side. Pre-existing (present before this PR; ship outcome unchanged vs old DENIED path), so not introduced/worsened, and depends on the unknown denial-record shape carrying input — hence PLAUSIBLE — but the fix is asymmetric relative to its own stated hardening goal. Remedy: collect the denied tool's name field and match on that, mirroring tool_use_names.

phase3_findings.summary: Stale comment at the raw-tool_use dump contradicts the now name-scoped match: 'the name-agnostic ... match above trusts that the token only appears via the real attempt' describes exactly the pre-#1527 vulnerable assumption the PR removed.
phase3_findings.detail: After the fix sw_attempted keys on the recorded tool_use name (names_text), so the match no longer 'trusts that the token only appears via the real attempt' — that trust is what allowed the ToolSearch false positive. Diff-untouched but adjacent to the changed logic; behavior-inert prose, but it actively misdescribes the security-relevant match. Reword to state the match keys on the tool_use name and the dump lets an operator confirm the harness's actual ScheduleWakeup name.

phase3_findings.detail: The shipped compute_verdict deleted the control_before AND control_after REMOVED branch: absence-of-attempt with both controls now yields INCONCLUSIVE, and REMOVED requires a permission_denials record with no attempt. Update to: REMOVED = a permission_denials record naming ScheduleWakeup with no registered tool_use attempt; no-attempt-no-denial = INCONCLUSIVE; controls only confirm progress past Action 2.

phase4_1_report.rationale: Three Important findings tied to the shipped change: (1) the fail-open hardening #1527 targets is left asymmetric — sw_denied still substring-matches the whole denial JSON, the exact vector fixed on the attempt side, and it gates shipping; (2) a stale Python comment at the raw-dump now describes the removed vulnerable assumption; (3) a stale matcher-probe.yml header contradicts the verdict logic this PR ships.
